title: Dragon/CoCo, Model 100, Apple III and STOS discovery
summary: Review thirteen fresh candidates, promote seven projects, and deepen the STOS component/runtime audit
notes: The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved source/target CPU areas, so no CPU value was inferred merely to satisfy a quota. Fresh GitHub repository/README searches were '"Dragon 32" disassembly source reconstruction', '"TRS-80 Model 100" disassembly development tooling', and '"Apple III" source disassembly homebrew tooling'; each narrow query returned no promotable candidate, so the repository route was broadened to 'dragon32', 'model100', and 'apple iii' without star, age, or recent-push filters. Thirteen canonical candidate URLs were screened and reviewed: seven promoted and six excluded. The STOS source/task queue was selected as an old partial component review and advanced with Falcon extension/runtime evidence. Read-only review: no compiler, assembler, ROM, disk/cassette image, emulator, hardware, firmware, driver, or destructive utility was run.

project.status: Preserved STOS BASIC compiler/interpreter and extension sources; Falcon DMA Sound runtime requirements verified

runtime_profiles.name: Falcon 030 DMA Sound Extension v2.2
runtime_profiles.notes: Primary manual states Falcon 030 only, 1/4/14 MB RAM and RGB/VGA/TV monitor.

identity.narrative: The repository remains the canonical STOS BASIC source collection and also preserves titled interpreter/compiler extensions, including GBP and the documented Falcon extension suite.

classification.narrative: This is recovered/preserved historical development-system source plus extension sources; it is not a binary-derived reimplementation or ordinary mirror.

source_cpu.narrative: The existing Motorola 68000 source CPU remains appropriate for the Atari ST core; the Falcon sound manual separately documents 68030 execution for that extension and does not replace the project-wide original architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The preserved compiler/interpreter target remains Motorola 68000-family ST software; the verified Falcon extension runtime is recorded as a variant requirement rather than broadening the canonical output CPU without evidence.

build.narrative: The inspected extension materials provide source and historical usage context, including full GBP interpreter/compiler source, but do not establish a complete reproducible modern build for the core STOS compiler/interpreter.
build.next_action: Trace the root/core build procedure and tool versions, then attempt a non-destructive build or locate an upstream reproducibility statement.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The Falcon DMA Sound manual explicitly requires an Atari Falcon 030, 1/4/14 MB RAM, RGB/VGA/TV display, STOS Basic and STOSFIX3; the lowest stated RAM value is captured without extrapolating to other STOS components.

ai.narrative: No explicit development-AI attribution was found in the inspected historical documentation/source materials; this does not establish non-use in later maintenance.

relationships.narrative: The Falcon suite and GBP Extension are now identified as titled components in the STOS repository, but the provenance boundary between original historical core sources and later adapted/system-interface trees remains incompletely documented.
relationships.next_action: Map the repository's orig and adapted source trees against named historical releases and extension authors before splitting or linking further component records.
